newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries edge up in Tokyo on dollar's rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries edge up in Tokyo on dollar's rise.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were higher in Tokyo afternoon trade on Friday in reaction to the dollar's rise against the yen.
Activity was extremely dull, with many Japanese investors sidelined. Sentiment remained mixed, with credit-tightening speculation continuing to limit active buying.
"The market is simply reacting to the dollar's rise this morning," a Japanese brokerage trader said. "But besides that currency factor, the market lacks driving forces."
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 97-1/32, yielding 6.86 percent, compared with 96-30/32 in New York on Thursday.
The June T-bond futures contract was at 110-14/32, up 4/32 from the previous close.
In New York, prices ended higher after early losses were erased and late short-covering lifted prices to session highs.
Traders said the market was nervous ahead of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting next week.
"Looking at the recent economic data, I think the Fed may not tighten at the FOMC meeting, but there is still a chance that it may hike the FF rate," the trader said.
"Such kind mixed speculation should keep the prices locked in tight ranges until the meeting."
